note: Append only log of prices read off a vendor pricing page. A new reading is a new entry with its own date. Nothing here is ever edited in place, because the point of the log is to show what was true when.

observations.billing: Monthly only. No annual option is offered anywhere on the pricing page, so an annual figure is twelve times the monthly one and carries no discount.
observations.model: Base price per tier plus a flat amount for every person on the team. The page asks how many cleaners and office managers are on the team and recalculates all three tiers. Verified linear across 0 to 12 people.

observations.model: Priced by number of locations cleaned, not headcount. Every plan includes unlimited users. All plans start at a minimum of fifteen locations, and the page bands locations at 1-15, 16-25, 26-30, 31-59 and 60+.

observations.verdict: The $30 quote is the entry price at the fifteen location minimum billed monthly, not a flat price. Headcount does not move it.

observations.verdict: The stored $43 at one user is correct, and the annualised $516, $780 and $1,704 at one, three and ten follow from $43 plus $11 a head.

observations.result: NO PRICE REACHABLE. The pricing page is a qualification wizard asking for industry, team size and goals. Worked through on a browser with no stored state it ends without displaying a figure. The only amount visible on a clean load is $0.
observations.whereTheOldFiguresCameFrom: Not from a completed wizard. $79, $189 and $329 were read out of plan-card markup and a hcpWebMcpComparePlans JavaScript variable present in the page source, in a browser session that could not reliably distinguish displayed content from hidden DOM. One later reading was served from a cookie named hcp_pricing_plan_cached, written by an earlier interaction in that same session, so it replayed a result rather than reading the page. $399 was never on the page in any form: it was arithmetic, $329 plus two users at $35.
observations.conclusion: None of the three can be dated as a reading, so all three are withdrawn and the row reads Could not confirm.
observations.ifItComesBack: If a plan table returns, the figures to look for are Basic 1 user, Essentials 5 users and Max 8 users with $35 per additional user. Treat them as unverified until seen on a clean session.

observations.readBy: Site owner, in their own browser. This client receives HTTP 403 from lawnprosoftware.com on both /price and /pricing, which is a network path rather than the site being down.

corrections.whatWasPublished: $39 a month at one, three and ten cleaners, on five guides and in the homepage docket, described as flat priced.
corrections.whatIsTrue: $39 is the Pro price with the team size calculator at its default of zero. The real Pro figures are $53 at one, $81 at three and $179 at ten, because the tier adds $14 a month for every person on the team.
corrections.cause: The calculator computes the prices in JavaScript and they are not in the page HTML, so a reading that did not drive the control saw only the zero position.
corrections.note: ZenMaid did not change its pricing. This is a correction to how the page was read, not a price movement.
corrections.noAugustEntry: This file was created on 2 October 2026 and has never held a 24 August observation, so there is no earlier entry to annotate. The August figures live only in the git history of the guides. The correction is recorded here rather than over anything.
